subtopics.name: Inflation and primordial perturbations
subtopics.scope: Dynamics of the inflationary epoch and the statistics of the scalar and tensor perturbations it seeds, including reheating and primordial non-Gaussianity.

subtopics.name: CMB anisotropies and spectral distortions
subtopics.scope: Temperature and polarization anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background and departures of its spectrum from a blackbody, from recombination through secondary effects.

subtopics.name: Thermal history and cosmological relics
subtopics.scope: Equilibrium and its breakdown in the hot early universe: neutrino decoupling, Big Bang nucleosynthesis, and the freeze-out or freeze-in of relic particles.

subtopics.name: Large-scale structure and halo formation
subtopics.scope: Growth of matter density fluctuations from the linear to the nonlinear regime, and the abundance, clustering and internal structure of dark matter halos.

subtopics.name: Intergalactic medium and cosmic reionization
subtopics.scope: The thermal and ionization state of diffuse gas between galaxies, the absorption and emission signatures it leaves, and the reionization of hydrogen and helium.

subtopics.name: Gravitational lensing across mass scales
subtopics.scope: Deflection of light by stars, galaxies, clusters and the cosmic web, including image configurations, magnification, time delays and cosmic shear statistics.

subtopics.name: Black hole perturbations and quasinormal modes
subtopics.scope: Linear response of black hole spacetimes to test fields and metric perturbations, including ringdown spectra, tidal response, superradiance and absorption.

subtopics.name: Compact binary dynamics and gravitational waves
subtopics.scope: Conservative and dissipative dynamics of inspiraling black hole and neutron star binaries, and the gravitational waveforms and fluxes they emit.

subtopics.name: Modified and alternative theories of gravity
subtopics.scope: Extensions of general relativity such as scalar-tensor, f(R), Horndeski and massive gravity, their black hole and cosmological solutions, and their observational constraints.

subtopics.name: Neutron stars and dense matter
subtopics.scope: Structure, oscillations, magnetospheres and thermal and rotational evolution of neutron stars and pulsars as probes of matter above nuclear density.

subtopics.name: Accretion flows onto compact objects
subtopics.scope: Hydrodynamics and MHD of gas accreting onto black holes, neutron stars and white dwarfs, from spherical Bondi flow to thin and advection-dominated disks and their winds.

subtopics.name: Relativistic outflows and particle acceleration
subtopics.scope: Jets, gamma-ray bursts, pulsar winds and other relativistic flows, the shocks and reconnection that accelerate particles in them, and the resulting non-thermal emission and cosmic rays.

subtopics.name: Stellar interiors, oscillations and tides
subtopics.scope: Hydrostatic structure and evolution of stars, including convection and rotation, the global oscillation modes probed by asteroseismology, and tidal interaction in close binaries.

subtopics.name: Solar and stellar magnetohydrodynamics
subtopics.scope: Generation, transport and dissipation of magnetic fields in the Sun and other stars, including dynamos, flux tubes, coronal heating, MHD waves and magnetized winds.

subtopics.name: Galactic dynamics and stellar systems
subtopics.scope: Gravitational dynamics of galaxies and star clusters, including equilibrium distribution functions, orbits, disk instabilities, dynamical friction and collisional relaxation.

subtopics.name: Star formation and interstellar medium
subtopics.scope: Physics of the multiphase interstellar gas and its gravitational collapse into stars, including turbulence, thermal instability, magnetic support and protostellar collapse.

techniques.name: Gauge-invariant cosmological perturbation theory
techniques.scope: Linearizing the Einstein, fluid and Boltzmann equations about an FRW background in gauge-invariant variables to get growth rates, transfer functions and conserved quantities on super- and sub-horizon scales.

techniques.name: Mode functions, Bogoliubov coefficients, in-in correlators
techniques.scope: Quantizing fields on expanding or black hole backgrounds, solving their mode equations, and computing particle production, power spectra or higher-point correlators with Bogoliubov transformations and the in-in formalism.

techniques.name: Boltzmann and Fokker-Planck kinetic equations
techniques.scope: Solving rate equations, moment hierarchies or diffusion equations for phase-space distributions to get freeze-out abundances, Kompaneets spectral evolution or momentum-space diffusion.

techniques.name: Post-Newtonian and multipolar expansions
techniques.scope: Expanding systematically in v/c and in multipole moments to compute the conservative dynamics, radiated fluxes and far-zone fields of gravitating systems.

techniques.name: Geodesic and effective-potential orbit analysis
techniques.scope: Reducing motion in symmetric spacetimes or potentials to effective potentials through conserved quantities, giving circular-orbit radii, epicyclic frequencies, precession rates, deflection angles and capture cross sections.

techniques.name: WKB, eikonal and geometric-optics approximations
techniques.scope: Short-wavelength asymptotics of wave equations to get mode spectra, transmission and tunnelling factors, eikonal quasinormal frequencies and light propagation.

techniques.name: Sturm-Liouville eigenmode problems and shooting
techniques.scope: Casting oscillation or perturbation equations with physical boundary conditions as eigenvalue problems, solved analytically in limits or by shooting, continued fractions or spectral methods.

techniques.name: Matched asymptotic and multiple-scale expansions
techniques.scope: Joining inner and outer solutions across widely separated scales, or separating fast and slow time scales, to get leading corrections, boundary layers and secular evolution.

techniques.name: Self-similar solutions and shock jump conditions
techniques.scope: Reducing PDEs to ODEs through scaling symmetry (blast waves, collapse, winds) and joining regions with Newtonian or relativistic Rankine-Hugoniot conditions.

techniques.name: Linear stability and dispersion-relation analysis
techniques.scope: Perturbing an equilibrium with plane-wave or normal-mode ansatzes to derive dispersion relations, growth rates and critical thresholds such as the Jeans, Toomre, magnetorotational and thermal instabilities.

techniques.name: Hydrostatic equilibrium and polytropic models
techniques.scope: Solving the Lane-Emden, TOV or isothermal-sphere equations, together with virial and scaling arguments, to get mass-radius relations, maximum masses and structural constants.

techniques.name: Hamiltonian, action-angle and secular perturbation theory
techniques.scope: Using canonical transformations, orbit averaging and resonance analysis to compute precession rates, secular oscillations such as von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai cycles, resonance widths and diffusion coefficients.

techniques.name: Gaussian random field and excursion-set statistics
techniques.scope: Computing power spectra, correlation functions, variances, and peak or threshold statistics of Gaussian or weakly non-Gaussian fields with Wick's theorem, window functions and barrier-crossing arguments.

techniques.name: Radiative processes and radiative transfer
techniques.scope: Deriving emissivities, absorption coefficients, spectra and optical depths for synchrotron, Compton, bremsstrahlung and line processes, and solving the transfer equation in simple geometries.
